entries.title: Computed hash is required before it can exist
entries.description: The canonical schema says every listed field is required, including source.content_hash, and step 3 validates every per-type registry file against that schema. But source.content_hash is described as computed during install in step 2, while the same per-type registries are initially hand-written. This makes a clean P1 registry either invalid before install or forces humans to maintain generated hashes by hand.

entries.title: Status lifecycle conflicts with registry source of truth
entries.description: The spec says per-type registries are the only declaration surface and every record includes status, but it also says the installer refuses to mark a capability installed until doctor passes and records failing capabilities as broken. It does not define whether the installer mutates hand-edited registries, writes status only to generated capabilities.yml, or treats status as derived runtime state. Without that boundary, AC5 cannot be implemented deterministically.

entries.title: One required schema shape overfits all capability types
entries.description: The canonical schema says every listed field is required unless noted, including install.command, install.args, provides.tools, requires.commands, and harness_targets. That shape is plausible for MCPs and executable commands but not for rules, pure documentation skills, libraries, or hooks that may not expose tools or have a PATH command. This will either force meaningless placeholder values or cause valid capability types to fail schema validation.

entries.title: Secret grep can miss realistic registry leaks
entries.description: AC11 only specifies a regex for key names followed by scalar-looking values. YAML secrets can appear in list values, nested env maps, quoted multi-line strings, command args, URLs with credentials, or innocuous keys like value. The current gate is useful as a smoke test but not enough to support the stronger claim that MCP records never contain literal secrets.

entries.title: Dry-run write semantics are undefined
entries.description: Several validations depend on install --dry-run producing deterministic outputs and diffs, but the install contract defines real writes to registries, adapters, lock files, and status. It is not specified whether dry-run writes to a temp tree, prints a plan, or materializes generated files somewhere stable. This makes AC2 and AC6 hard to test consistently.

entries.title: Disabled normalized records still require content_hash
entries.description: The normalized schema says source.content_hash is required for capabilities.yml and lock entries. But the install contract says records with status disabled are skipped before source resolution and hash computation, then pass through as status disabled. That leaves disabled normalized records unable to satisfy final normalized validation unless the implementation violates the short-circuit rule by hashing them anyway.

entries.title: Pre-doctor adapter emission can leave empty adapters
entries.description: Step 5 writes harness adapters before doctor has converted records from declared to installed, while emitters exclude every status other than installed. In a real install, an interruption or doctor crash between steps 5 and 7 can leave .codex/config.toml, CLAUDE.md, and AGENTS.md regenerated with the new run's installed set missing or empty. That contradicts the goal of deterministic adapters reflecting known-good installed capabilities.

entries.title: Forbidden fields are ambiguously allowed when empty
entries.description: The per-type table says some fields are forbidden, but the prose says empty maps/lists are permitted where the table says optional or forbidden. That makes forbidden mean either absent-only or present-but-empty depending on the implementer. JSON Schema enforcement will diverge unless the spec states the exact accepted shape.

entries.title: Nested schema paths are encoded as dotted required keys
entries.description: The normalized schema section says disabled records forbid doctor.last_run_status using `{ not: { required: ["doctor.last_run_status"] } }`. JSON Schema `required` checks literal property names at the current object level; it does not interpret dotted field paths. If implementers follow the spec literally, the load-bearing disabled-record invariant can fail open for nested doctor fields.

entries.title: Adapter promotion is not actually all-or-nothing
entries.description: Step 8 calls `os.replace` for each adapter and then writes generated registry artifacts, but labels the phase all-or-nothing. A crash after replacing `.codex/config.toml` and before replacing `CLAUDE.md` can leave a mixed adapter set. AC14 only faults before promotion, so it does not test the partial-promotion state the text claims to prevent.

entries.title: Conditional oneOf branches validate vacuously
entries.description: The normalized schema fragment uses `oneOf` containing `if`/`then` branches without an `else` or a branch-local `required: ["status"]` plus `const` guard. In JSON Schema, when an `if` condition is false and no `else` is present, that subschema still validates. As written, a valid `status: disabled` record can satisfy the disabled branch and also vacuously satisfy the non-disabled branch, causing `oneOf` to fail; the same risk applies in reverse for installed/broken/declared records.
